content_sections.heading: IIT Madras Principal Project Officer Vacancy Details 2026
content_sections.text: The post is temporary and is based at IIT Madras, Chennai. FREEJOBALERT DAILY QUIZ Preparing for Govt Exams? Test Yourself! 25 Questions · 20 Minutes · Instant Score Take Today's Free Quiz →

content_sections.heading: IIT Madras Principal Project Officer Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: All eligibility conditions are checked as on the closing date for online applications, 12 November 2026. You need one of these: A Master's degree in engineering with 10 years of experience A Master's degree in science with 15 years of experience A Ph.D. with 3 years of experience Only relevant experience gained after the minimum qualifying degree is counted. Technical experience: Hands-on familiarity with fabrication processes and equipment, such as lithography, deposition, wet or plasma etching, thermal processing, or metrology. Core capabilities: Cleanroom safety, SOP implementation, maintenance and troubleshooting, staff and user coordination, and technical documentation. Professional skills: Strong organization, communication and practical problem-solving, and proficiency in spreadsheets and reporting tools. 3–5 years of relevant and exclusive experience in a semiconductor nanofabrication cleanroom facility will be considered an added advantage. Experience managing, or helping to manage, a shared research or fabrication facility, including vendor coordination, facility administration and funded-project reporting. You must be a citizen of India. Persons who migrated from Pakistan intending to settle permanently in India, and subjects of Nepal, are also eligible. They will need a certificate of eligibility from the Government of India, applied for through the Ministry of Home Affairs. For exceptionally outstanding candidates, the minimum qualification and/or experience can be relaxed. For SC/ST candidates, the institute may relax the experience requirement if not enough candidates from these communities with the required experience are likely to apply. The prescribed qualifications are the minimum. Having a higher qualification does not by itself get you an interview call. Check the official notification for the full eligibility details of the post.

content_sections.heading: Duties of the Principal Project Officer
content_sections.text: The Principal Project Officer will take substantial responsibility for day-to-day technical and operational management. The work is done with faculty and technical staff to support safe, reliable and efficient fabrication and characterisation activities. Facility operations: Coordinate daily activities, equipment bookings, user access and competing requests, and tell users clearly when equipment is available or down. Equipment reliability: Support troubleshooting and preventive maintenance, keep service records, and coordinate vendors, repairs and spare parts. Safety and protocols: Implement cleanroom and laboratory safety procedures, maintain SOPs, support user induction, and make sure established protocols are followed. Staff and user coordination: Work with technical staff, students, faculty and external users, and organise training and equipment authorisation with the responsible teams. Records and administration: Maintain usage logs, inventory and consumables records, and support procurement documentation, billing and payment follow-up. Project documentation: Prepare technical and progress reports, track deliverables, and maintain financial and supporting records with the project and administrative teams. Stakeholder communication: Deal with faculty, vendors, external users and funding-agency or ministry officials, and support meetings and project reviews. Operational improvement: Find recurring process and coordination gaps, and improve scheduling, documentation and service continuity.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Candidates are shortlisted for a test and/or interview based on the information in their online applications. The institute may limit the number of candidates called for a written test, skill test or interview to a reasonable number. It decides this on qualifications, on experience that is higher in level and more relevant than the minimum, and on other academic achievements. The institute decides how applicants are screened and tested for shortlisting and selection. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. All contact is by e-mail. Applicants already working in any project at IIT Madras must apply through proper channel. Otherwise they must produce a No-Objection Certificate at the document verification, test or interview. Without it, they will not be allowed to appear.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: The post is temporary and purely on contract. Duration: initially one year, later extendable based on performance. Completing the contract gives no right to further extension, regularization or permanency at the institute. Work location: IIT Madras, Chennai. Documents and antecedents may be verified at any time, including during service. Services are liable to be terminated if documents are fake or information was suppressed.

faq.question: Q1. Can I apply with a Master's degree in science?
faq.answer: Yes, if you also have 15 years of experience. With a Master's degree in engineering you need 10 years, and with a Ph.D. you need 3 years.

faq.question: Q2. Is cleanroom experience compulsory?
faq.answer: No. 3–5 years of relevant and exclusive experience in a semiconductor nanofabrication cleanroom facility is preferred and counts as an added advantage. Hands-on familiarity with processes such as lithography, deposition, etching, thermal processing or metrology is listed under the post's experience requirements.

faq.question: Q3. Is this a permanent job?
faq.answer: No. It is a temporary contract post, initially for one year and extendable based on performance. Completing the contract gives no right to regularization or permanency.

faq.question: Q4. Where is the job based?
faq.answer: At IIT Madras, Chennai, in the Department of Electrical Engineering. The co-ordinator is Prof. Shanti Bhattacharya.

faq.question: Q5. Do I need to send a hard copy of the application?
faq.answer: No. Keep a printout of the online application and bring it if you are called for document verification, a test or an interview.

faq.question: Q6. I work on a project at IIT Madras. What extra do I need?
faq.answer: Apply through proper channel, or bring a No-Objection Certificate to the document verification, test or interview. Without the NOC you will not be allowed to appear.

faq.question: Q7. Which date is used to check my eligibility?
faq.answer: The closing date for online applications, 12 November 2026, is the crucial date for every eligibility condition.

faq.question: Q8. Whom do I contact if the application will not submit?
faq.answer: E-mail [email protected] or [email protected], or call 044- 2257 8843 on working days between 9.00 AM and 05.30 PM. Only technical issues are handled.

faq.question: Q9. Can SC/ST candidates get any relaxation?
faq.answer: Yes. The institute may relax the required experience for SC/ST candidates if it finds that not enough candidates from these communities with that experience are likely to be available.
